title: India Delivers Strong Diplomatic Rebuttal to Pakistan's Terrorism Accusations at UNGA
detail: India delivered a pointed rebuttal at the 81st UN General Assembly session on September 26, 2026, countering Pakistan's terrorism-related accusations and accusing Islamabad of 'hypocritical homilies about democratic rights.' India's delegation rejected what it described as bad-faith accusations from a state it holds responsible for cross-border terrorism, while calling attention to Pakistan's own democratic and human rights record. The exchange underscores the ongoing bilateral deep freeze following the May 2025 ceasefire — with no ambassadors, no formal trade, and the Indus Waters Treaty still in abeyance.

media.caption: India's UNGA delegation responds to Pakistan's accusations at the UN General Assembly

title: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif Raises Kashmir at UNGA, Credits Trump for 2025 Conflict Intervention
detail: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif addressed the 81st UN General Assembly on September 26, 2026, raising the Kashmir dispute and calling for self-determination under UN resolutions. Sharif credited US President Trump for a 'timely intervention' that helped end the May 2025 India-Pakistan military confrontation, framing US mediation as critical to preventing escalation. The remarks are Pakistan's first major multilateral platform statement since the ceasefire and signal Islamabad's intent to keep Kashmir and the conflict's aftermath on the international agenda despite India's insistence that bilateral issues must be resolved without third-party involvement.

media.caption: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif addresses the UN General Assembly, raising Kashmir and crediting Trump
